373f287c.yl: Yield: 10 portions × 120 g (3 meatballs) · Portion: 120 g
c: Batch · 30 meatballs × 50 g raw · Cooked yield ≈ 1200 g
Dice the onion finely; mince the garlic.
Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for 5 min.
Combine all ingredients except the oil at ≤4 °C. Mix briefly until just bound; do not overwork.
Portion at 50 g and shape into even balls (30 pcs).
Place on a lightly oiled perforated GN tray.
Convection 185 °C, 0% humidity, 13–15 min, to a core of 75 °C.
Rest for 2 min. Serve, or finish in a hot sauce held at ≥75 °C.
Portion 3 meatballs (120 g) per plate at ≥63 °C.

c: Scrub the mussels and remove the beards; discard any with broken shells or that stay open when tapped.
Steam in a covered pan with a splash of water for 3–4 min until opened; discard any that stay closed.
Remove the top shells; loosen the meat in the bottom shell. Cool to below 5 °C within 90 min if not baking at once.
Mix all ingredients until smooth. Keep at 0–4 °C.
Arrange the mussels on a tray; top each with spicy mayo and grated cheese.
Bake at 220 °C convection (or under the salamander) for 5–7 min until golden; core 75 °C.
Sprinkle with spring onion; serve hot with a lemon wedge.

Coat each tender: dry mix → wet batter → dry mix, pressing the final coat on firmly. Leave in the dry mix until frying.

Drain on a rack, not on paper. Serve immediately with the sauce of the day.

c: Partly freeze the meat (−2 °C) and cut into cubes.
Mince 70% finely; chop 30% coarsely for texture.
Mix with the salt, sugar, spices, egg, cream and corn starch until homogeneous. Keep the mix at 0–4 °C.
Form 25 nuggets of 35–40 g; chill 30 min at 0–4 °C.
Dry mix: combine the flour, potato starch, salt, pepper, paprika and garlic powder.
Wet mix: whisk the buttermilk, eggs and water.
Bread each nugget: dry mix, wet mix, dry mix again. Rest 10 min.
Fry at 160 °C for 3–4 min; rest 3 min.
Fry again at 185 °C for 60–90 s until golden and crisp, to a core temperature of 75 °C.
Drain on a rack; season lightly with salt.
Serve 5 nuggets (≈225 g) per portion immediately.

c: Pierce the aubergines. Roast whole at 220 °C hot air on a perforated tray, 35–40 min, turning once, until the skins blister and the flesh collapses.
Roast the peppers on a separate tray at 220 °C hot air, 20 min, until blackened in patches.
Steam the peppers in a covered GN for 15 min; peel, deseed and drain.
Split the aubergines, scoop out the flesh and drain in a colander for 30 min without pressing.
Chop both by hand to a coarse, even texture. Do not blend.
Crush the garlic to a paste. Fold in the garlic, salt and sugar; add the vinegar, then the oil in three additions.
Chill to ≤4 °C within 90 min; rest 2 h at 0–4 °C. Fold in the parsley on the day of service.
Portion 60 g per plate. Serve at 4–8 °C.

Shape into cylinders or balls; seal well.

c: Batch · 10 portions · from 1600 g fillet as purchased

Use chilled fillet, or frozen fillet thawed at 0–4 °C for 12–14 h (never in water or at room temperature). Remove pin bones and membrane, rinse in cold water and pat dry. 1600 g fillet as purchased gives about 1500 g trimmed. Hake or pollock can replace cod at the same weights.
Cut into pieces 3–4 cm wide, 2–3 pieces (150 g) per portion. Season with the salt and pepper, sprinkle with the lemon juice and hold covered at 0–4 °C for 10–15 min.
Just before frying, pat dry, dust in the flour and shake off the excess.
Sift the flour with the starch, baking powder and salt. Add the egg and the ice-cold sparkling water; whisk briefly to the thickness of sour cream. Small lumps are fine.
Mix just before frying, keep on ice and use within 30 min.
Heat the oil in the fryer to 175–180 °C.
Dip each piece in the batter, let the excess drip off and lower it into the oil away from you. Fry 3–4 min until golden. Do not overload: at most 1 part fish to 4 parts oil.

Core temperature at least 75 °C. Drain on a rack for 30–60 s (frying loss about 21 %). Plate 170 g fish on a warmed plate with 2 lemon wedges (16 g). Serve at once, at not less than 65 °C; tartare sauce and garnish per their own TTKs.
